brief.headline: Fix the 40% return rate first, then push price toward ₹0.65–0.80/pc and tighten payment to 15 days

priceAsk.summary: Target ₹0.65–0.80/pc for the 28 mm PP cap at higher volume
priceAsk.basis: Market asking price for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc. The market verdict says there is modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec — so ask them to match that band.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days after receipt to 15 days after receipt
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: This frees up ₹6817 in cash for us

brief.financialLeverage: This supplier does not publish financials, so we have no view on their profit, debt, or cash situation. Our ₹1.66 L annual spend is tiny — we are not a make-or-break customer for them. That limits how hard we can push on price alone. The real leverage is the 40% return rate: they are bleeding cost and credibility with us, so lead with fixing quality and paperwork, then tie better terms to fewer problems.

evidence.point: Four out of ten deliveries from them get sent back
Our total annual spend with them is very small
Current payment term is 30 days after we receive the goods
Market asking price for a 28 mm PP cap runs ₹0.55–1.20 per piece, typically ₹0.85–0.95
At higher volume or looser spec, the market sees room down to ₹0.65–0.80 per piece
evidence.figure: modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter; does pharma bottles, caps and preforms; top second-source candidate with ₹2569.83 Cr revenue and B (65/100) health score

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers and pharma; strong and profitable — a robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited (lead to qualify)
alternates.why: A manufacturer lead from public research (India-Pan, medium confidence) — verify capability and pricing before RFQ

risks: The 40% return rate is costing us time, rework and inventory headaches — if it does not improve fast, we may need to switch supplier mid-year.
We have no financial data on them, so we cannot tell if they are stable or stretched — keep a close eye on delivery consistency.
Our ₹1.66 L spend gives us almost no customer weight — they may simply walk away if we push too hard on price alone.
The market backups (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) are leads to qualify, not approved sources yet — do not threaten to switch unless Manjushree or Mold-Tek are ready.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We need to talk about the 40% return rate — it is costing both of us money, and we want to work with you to fix it before we look at price and terms.
